## Review: `UnixSocketTransport.swift` (86 lines)

**Bug 1 — EINTR not handled on read/write (lines 30, 44):** Both `read()` and `write()` treat any `n < 0` as `ioFailed(errno)`. When `errno == EINTR` (signal interrupted), the call must retry instead of throwing. On Linux this will break valid exchanges under `SIGCHLD` or timer signals.

**Bug 2 — `write()` return of 0 treated as fatal (line 31):** `n <= 0` makes `n == 0` throw `ioFailed`. On stream sockets `write()` returning 0 is non-fatal (kernel accepted 0 bytes without error); this should `continue` the write loop.

**No O(n²) re-parsing:** `KistControlFraming.decode` only checks the 4-byte length prefix each iteration (constant time). The `consumed` value is unused but harmless per-connection.

**No fd leak:** `defer { close(fd) }` at line 70 runs on all paths after the guard on `fd < 0`.

**Framing sound:** Length prefix correct, oversized frames rejected fail-closed, partial reads handled cleanly.
